age.evidence: Male Swiss mice (18 -22 weeks old; 35 -45 g)

sex.evidence: only male mice were employed in this study... A total of 136 animals were initially subjected to the inescapable stress to select a total of 75 helpless mice.

dosing.evidence: Drugs were diluted in 0.9% NaCl and administered acutely via intraperitoneal injection (i.p.) 24 h before the test session of the learned helplessness model. ... The doses of DMT fumarate 25 and 10 mg/kg used were equivalent to 19.1 and 7.6 mg/kg, respectively, of DMT free-base.
Drugs were diluted in 0.9% NaCl and administered acutely via intraperitoneal injection (i.p.)

group_housing.evidence: Mice were housed in groups of up to eight per cage... until the beginning of experiments. Step 2: mice were housed individually 7 days before the beginning of the learned helplessness model (only Step 1 LH cohort remained group-housed, 5-8 per cage).

day_night_flipped.evidence: 12:12 h light--dark cycle, lights on at 6:00 a.m.; Sessions were conducted during the light phase under low ambient light.

assays.assay_name: Gross behaviour in home cage (acute post-injection observation)
assays.assay_description: Single-housed helpless mice video-recorded in their home cage 10-15 min after i.p. injection (5 min); manual scoring of rearing counts, lid-climbing time, grooming time and time stopped.

setup_habituation.evidence: Recording took place in the animal's own home cage; no separate apparatus habituation described.

setup_restrain.evidence: Immediately after drug administration, mice were placed in the home cage located in the animal facility

food_restriction.evidence: home cage; food and water available ad libitum

water_restriction.evidence: home cage; food and water available ad libitum

time_to_assay.evidence: the animal behavior was video recorded in the interval between 10 and 15 min after treatments

sample_size.evidence: Table 1 (Freezing; lid-climbing; rearings; grooming): vehicle 16, S-ketamine 10 mg/kg 9, S-ketamine 30 mg/kg 5, DMT 10 mg/kg 12, DMT 25 mg/kg 6

outcomes.summary: DMT at 10 and 25 mg/kg acutely reduced exploratory behaviours (rearing, lid-climbing) and grooming and increased time stopped 10 min post-injection; S-ketamine only altered behaviour at 30 mg/kg.
outcomes.statistics: ANOVA, Dunnett's test, rearings: F(4,43) = 7.81; lid-climbing time: F(4,43) = 3.66; grooming time: F(4,43) = 4.39; stopped time: F(4,43) = 4.20, p < 0.05 for all
outcomes.evidence: DMT at both doses tested, 10 and 25 mg/kg, significantly reduced exploratory behaviors (such as rearing counts and time of lid-climbing) and increased time stopped

B1_num_measures.evidence: The behaviors measured were: rearing counts, time spent lid-climbing in the home cage, grooming (i.e., self-cleaning), and time stopped

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Videos were used to manually quantify gross behaviors... by a blinded experimenter

E1_environment_type.evidence: mice were placed in the home cage located in the animal facility

E8_food_water.evidence: home cage testing; food and water available ad libitum

D1_continuity.evidence: video recorded in the interval between 10 and 15 min after treatments

D2_session_duration.evidence: measured 10 min post-drug injection for 5 min

D3_recording_days.evidence: Single recording on the injection day

assays.assay_description: Two-compartment shuttle box (50 × 30 × 30 cm, grid floor). After two inescapable-shock induction days, screening session (day 3; 5-min exploration + 30 escapable shock trials) pre-drug and test session 24 h post-drug (day 4). Escape frequency and escape latency (blocks of 15 trials). Run in group-housed (vehicle, S-ketamine 10, DMT 10) and single-housed (vehicle, S-ketamine 10/30, DMT 10/25) cohorts.

application_type.evidence: Helpless mice were treated with vehicle, S-ketamine or DMT... i.p. immediately after the screening session

setup_habituation.evidence: Mice underwent two induction sessions... confined to a single compartment; with the guillotine door closed, animals explored the shuttle box for 5 min (light off) before screening

setup_restrain.evidence: Avoidance was defined as crossing to the opposite compartment

food_restriction.evidence: No food in the shuttle box during testing

water_restriction.evidence: No water in the shuttle box during testing

time_to_assay.evidence: Twenty-four hours after drug administration (day 4), mice underwent a test session identical to the screening session

sample_size.evidence: Table 1: group-housed vehicle 09, S-ketamine 10 06, DMT 10 08; single-housed vehicle 16, S-ketamine 10 08, S-ketamine 30 05, DMT 10 10, DMT 25 05

outcomes.summary: In group-housed helpless mice, DMT 10 mg/kg (like S-ketamine 10 mg/kg) increased escape frequency and reduced escape latency 24 h post-injection. In single-housed mice neither drug, at any dose, reversed helplessness.
outcomes.statistics: Group-housed escapes: ANOVA, Dunnett's, F(2,20) = 4.10, p = 0.03; latency: RM ANOVA treatment F(2,80) = 7.60, p < 0.05, sessions F(3,80) = 14.70, p < 0.05, interaction F(6,80) = 2.41, p < 0.05; single-housed: p > 0.05 for escapes and latency
outcomes.evidence: A significant increase in the frequency of escape in the test session was detected in S-ketamine- and DMT-treated mice compared to control (Fig. 3c, ANOVA, Dunnett's test, F(2,20) = 4.10, p = 0.03)... the treatment with S-ketamine and DMT, even at higher doses, did not abolish the helpless behavior in single-housed mice

B1_num_measures.evidence: Escape latency and the frequency of escapes were recorded

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Escape latencies in the screening and test sessions, analyzed in blocks of 15 escapable footshock trials

B5_social.evidence: Animals were individually placed in acrylic shuttle box

B6_cognitive.evidence: Learned helplessness paradigm with cued escapable shock trials (learned escape/avoidance)

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Animal mobility during escapable sessions... was manually scored by an experimenter blinded to treatment conditions

E1_environment_type.evidence: acrylic shuttle box (50 × 30 × 30 cm) with a stainless-steel grid floor

E6_spatial.evidence: divided into two compartments by a guillotine door (12 × 25 cm)

E7_social_context.evidence: Animals were individually placed in acrylic shuttle box

D1_continuity.evidence: screening session (day 3) and test session (day 4), both reported (Fig. 3, 4)

D2_session_duration.evidence: Total session duration not explicitly stated (30 trials, mean ITI 20 s)

D4_baseline.evidence: Helpless mice were assigned to treatment groups such that there were no baseline differences in the number of escapes and escape latency during screening

D5_followup.evidence: Twenty-four hours after drug administration (day 4), mice underwent a test session (>=24 h criterion met)

assays.assay_description: Home-cage two-bottle choice (2% sucrose vs water) for 12 h after 4 h water deprivation; bottles weighed. Measured % sucrose preference and total liquid intake at baseline (pre-stress), 48 h and 5 days post-drug in single-housed helpless mice.

setup_habituation.evidence: animals were habituated to two bottles (A and B), both containing 2% sucrose solution, for ~12 h during the dark phase

setup_restrain.evidence: Testing in home cage of individually housed mice

food_restriction.evidence: Only water deprivation described; After the test, mice were returned to ad libitum food and water access

water_restriction.evidence: mice were deprived of water for 4 h immediately before re-exposure to the bottles

time_to_assay.evidence: baseline (before learned helplessness model), 48 h (or 3 days) and 5 days after drug-treatment

sample_size.evidence: Table 1 % sucrose preference: vehicle 09, S-ketamine 10 07, S-ketamine 30 04, DMT 10 07, DMT 25 06

outcomes.summary: Vehicle helpless mice showed reduced sucrose preference 5 days post-treatment (not at 48 h); DMT (10 and 25 mg/kg) and S-ketamine prevented this reduction. Total liquid intake unchanged except increased by S-ketamine 30 mg/kg.
outcomes.statistics: RM ANOVA, Dunnett's test, F(2,16) = 3.71, p = 0.04; total liquid ingestion F(2,6) = 40.28, p < 0.05
outcomes.evidence: both S-ketamine and DMT (at all doses tested) significantly prevented the reduction of sucrose preference observed in the control group 5 days after treatments (Fig. 5a, RM ANOVA, Dunnett's test, F(2,16) = 3.71, p = 0.04)

B1_num_measures.evidence: % sucrose preference (Fig. 5a) and total liquid ingestion (Fig. 5b)

B4_ethological.evidence: Fluid intake by bottle weight, not ethological acts

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Bottles were weighed before and after testing

E1_environment_type.evidence: Testing was performed in helpless individually housed mice; ...to adapt to 2 bottles in the home cage

E8_food_water.evidence: Animals were then given 12 h of access to one bottle containing 2% sucrose (bottle A) and another containing water (bottle B)

D1_continuity.evidence: performed at three time points: baseline, 48 h and 5 days after drug-treatment

D2_session_duration.evidence: Animals were then given 12 h of access

D3_recording_days.evidence: baseline, 48 h and 5 days = 3 recording days

D4_baseline.evidence: Baseline measurements were taken after the sucrose solution habituation period, and before footshock stress sessions

assays.assay_description: Mice suspended by tail (>50 cm above floor) for 6 min; immobility manually scored during final 4 min. Repeated at 28 h, 120 h and 192 h post-drug in single-housed helpless mice.

setup_restrain.evidence: Mice were suspended by the tail using adhesive tape placed ~1 cm from the tip

time_to_assay.evidence: The TST was performed at three time points: 28 h (2 h following the learned helplessness test session), 120 h, and 192 h after drug-treatment

sample_size.evidence: Table 1 immobility 28 h: vehicle 13, S-ketamine 10 09, S-ketamine 30 05, DMT 10 12, DMT 25 06; 120/192 h: 10, 07, 05, 05, 06

outcomes.summary: S-ketamine 30 mg/kg reduced immobility at 28 h only, whereas DMT 10 mg/kg reduced (trend-level in Results) immobility with effects persisting up to 8 days post-injection.
outcomes.statistics: Mixed effects analysis, Dunnett's post-hoc test, treatment effect, F(4,43) = 3.56, p < 0.05
outcomes.evidence: S-ketamine (only at 30 mg/kg) reduced the immobility time in helpless mice at 28 h after drug administration, while DMT 10 mg/kg trended to evoked a similar effect up to 8 days after drug injection (Fig. 5c; Mixed effects analysis, Dunnett's post-hoc test, treatment effect, F(4,43) = 3.56, p < 0.05)

B1_num_measures.evidence: immobility time (defined as the absence of escape-oriented movements)

B7_automated_classification.evidence: manually recorded during the final 4 min by an observer blinded to treatment conditions

B8_multivariate.evidence: Mixed effects analysis on single measure

E1_environment_type.evidence: suspended by the tail... at a height > 50 cm above the floor

D1_continuity.evidence: 28 h, 120 h, and 192 h after drug-treatment

D3_recording_days.evidence: Three recording days (28 h, 120 h, 192 h)

D5_followup.evidence: 28 h, 120 h and 192 h after drug-treatment

assays.assay_description: Square arena (40 × 40 × 40 cm), low red light, 30-min session ~30 h post-drug; ANY-maze tracking of total distance, distance in 5-min blocks, % centre time and % centre distance (first 10 min).

setup_restrain.evidence: Mice were individually placed in the center of a square arena... Spontaneous exploration was recorded

time_to_assay.evidence: The open field test was performed ~30 h after treatment with DMT, (S)-ketamine, or vehicle

sample_size.evidence: Table 1 Open field test: vehicle 15 (01 video-recording problems), S-ketamine 10 09, S-ketamine 30 05, DMT 10 12, DMT 25 06

outcomes.summary: DMT 10 mg/kg (not 25 mg/kg or S-ketamine) increased distance moved 30 h after injection, especially in the first 15 min, interpreted as reversal of stress-induced hypolocomotion; no change in centre exploration.
outcomes.statistics: 2-way ANOVA, Dunnett's: time effect F(5,251) = 82.08, p < 0.05, treatment effect F(4,251) = 11.12, p < 0.05; cumulative distance ANOVA F(4,43) = 2.78, p = 0.04; centre measures p > 0.05
outcomes.evidence: DMT 10 mg/kg, but not S-ketamine (at the doses tested), 30 h after administration significantly increased the spontaneous distance moved compared to vehicle-treated mice. This effect of DMT was particularly significant at the first 15 min of observation

B1_num_measures.evidence: Total distance moved..., the distance moved analyzed in blocks of 5 min, and time spent in and the distance moved into the center area

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: the distance moved analyzed in blocks of 5 min

B4_ethological.evidence: Locomotor distance and zone measures only

B7_automated_classification.evidence: analyzed with Anymaze® software (position tracking; score 0)

B8_multivariate.evidence: ANOVA only; Pearson correlation between two variables is not multivariate

E3_bedding.evidence: The arena was cleaned with 5% ethanol between trials; no bedding described

E6_spatial.evidence: Open field with virtual centre zone

D2_session_duration.evidence: Spontaneous exploration was recorded for 30 min

D5_followup.evidence: performed ~30 h after treatment (>=24 h post-dose)

assays.assay_description: Re-exposure to the LH shuttle box (door open, light on, no shocks) for 3 min at 5 and 8 days post-drug; % freezing manually scored.

application_type.evidence: Drug-treatment happened 24 h before the last escapable footshock session

setup_habituation.evidence: Prior exposures were conditioning (LH) sessions; no separate habituation described

setup_restrain.evidence: re-exposed to the same context (i.e., chamber) for 3 min, with the guillotine door open

time_to_assay.evidence: animal behavior was registered at 5 days and 8 days after drug-administration

sample_size.evidence: Table 1 % freezing (192 h): vehicle 10, S-ketamine 10 09, S-ketamine 30 05, DMT 10 05, DMT 25 06; DMT 10 as low as 04 at 120 h (table partially garbled)

outcomes.summary: DMT 10 mg/kg showed a non-significant trend toward reduced freezing at 5 days post-injection; S-ketamine had no effect.
outcomes.evidence: a reduced percentage of freezing time was observed in helpless mice injected with DMT 10 mg/kg but it did not reach the significance (Fig. 6f, Kruskal-Wallis test, p = 0.10, K = 4.54)

B6_cognitive.evidence: Fear memory was assessed... contextual memory test

B7_automated_classification.evidence: assessed manually by an experienced observer blinded to treatment conditions

E6_spatial.evidence: two-compartment shuttle box with the guillotine door open

D1_continuity.evidence: registered at 5 days and 8 days after drug-administration

D2_session_duration.evidence: re-exposed to the same context... for 3 min

D3_recording_days.evidence: Two test days (day 8 and day 11 of experiment)

assays.assay_description: 5-min free exploration starting on central platform, 5 days post-drug (30 min after CFC); manually scored % time in open arms and closed-arm entries/transitions.

setup_restrain.evidence: allowed to freely explore the apparatus for 5 min

time_to_assay.evidence: EPM test was conducted once 30 min after contextual fear conditioning in helpless mice 5 days after drug-administration

sample_size.evidence: Fig. 6d ANOVA F(2,18) (vehicle, DMT 10, DMT 25); Table 1: DMT 10 05, DMT 25 05 (01 outlier); S-ketamine groups 09 and 05 (data not shown)

outcomes.summary: DMT 10 and 25 mg/kg increased % time in open arms 5 days post-injection (anxiolytic-like); no change in closed-arm entries; S-ketamine ineffective.
outcomes.statistics: ANOVA, Dunnett's; F(2,18) = 4.13, p = 0.03; closed-arm entries p > 0.05
outcomes.evidence: DMT 10 and 25 mg/kg, but not S-ketamine 10 and 30 mg/kg (p > 0.05; data not shown), increased the time spent exploring the open arms (Fig. 6d, ANOVA, Dunnett's; F(2,18) = 4.13, p = 0.03)

outcomes.summary: Neither DMT nor S-ketamine altered latency to feed or food consumption in either the unfamiliar arena or the home cage 8 days post-injection.

judge_notes: Merged deepseek4's separate group-housed and single-housed learned helplessness entries into one LH assay (same paradigm, different housing cohort); n_total summed from Table 1 (23 + 44 = 67).
Retained 8 assays: gross home-cage behaviour, LH, SPT, TST, OFT, CFC, EPM, NSFB. All three candidates agreed on this set.
Corrected B1 score/category mismatches in gemma4 (e.g., '2-3' scored 2, '1' scored 1). Gross behaviour has 4 measures -> 4-6 (score 2); OFT has 4 measures -> 4-6 (score 2).
SPT D2 overridden to >6 h (score 3) and D6 = Yes: the paper states 12 h bottle access, which exceeds the 6-h cutoff. qwen and gemma4 had scored 61 min-6 h.
OFT D5 overridden to Yes: testing occurred ~30 h post-dose, which meets the >=24 h criterion. LH D5 also set to Yes because the test was run 24 h post-dose (rubric threshold is >=24 h).
LH D2 set to 0 with low confidence: the paper does not explicitly state total session duration.
Home-cage E3 (bedding) set to 0/low: bedding is never explicitly mentioned, and the rubric forbids inferring it. Two candidates had inferred bedding as present.
Gross behaviour E8 and food/water_restriction scored as accessible ('no' restriction) with medium confidence. Recording was in the home cage, and the paper states ad libitum food/water under housing.
group_housing set to 'no' with medium confidence: the rubric asks for housing during testing, and 7 of 8 assays used single-housed mice. The Step-1 LH cohort was group-housed.
OFT time_to_assay re-binned to short_term_1to7d (30 h) and NSFB to long_term_over7d (8 days = 11520 min). The LH 24 h test was binned early_2to24h, correcting gemma4's 'acute' label.
CFC E6 set to Multiple compartments: re-exposure was in the two-compartment shuttle box with the door open (2 of 3 candidates agreed).
Added S-ketamine as a second dosing entry (comparator compound) per the rubric's 'every compound' instruction. Sex n_male uses the 75 helpless mice that were treated and tested.
